data.description:
## Description

**What**: A user-invoked CLI command (`dso commit-override --reason="..."`) that authorizes a single subsequent commit to proceed despite a compliance-verifier hook block, with a durable audit record of the override.

**Why**: SC3 of the parent epic — a hard-blocking pre-commit gate is unsafe to deploy without an escape hatch for legitimate commits the gate gets wrong. This story is the release-blocking precondition: the override path must exist before SC1's gate is enabled by default in production.

**Scope**:
- IN: `dso commit-override --reason="<text>"` shim entry; one-shot semantics (override token consumed by next commit attempt only); audit record written to `$ARTIFACTS_DIR/commit-overrides.log` (JSON Lines, one record per use, listing missing-artifact set + user reason + timestamp); audit record also surfaced as a commit trailer or comment so it is visible in `git log`; agent-self-invocation refused (process lineage / TTY check); `dso commit-override` returns an error with a clear message when `dso-fbky` autonomous mode is active.
- OUT: bypassing reviewer-finding-driven blocks (this command composes with — does not bypass — `jira-dig-1673` reviewer override discipline); UI for browsing past overrides (later concern).

## Done Definitions

- When this story is complete, a user invoking `dso commit-override --reason="<text>"` followed by a single `git commit` clears that one commit even when the (yet-to-ship) compliance-verifier hook would otherwise block it; a second commit attempt without re-authorization is blocked again.
  ← Satisfies: "SC3 — Per-commit interactive override path"
- When this story is complete, every override invocation writes a durable audit record listing the missing artifacts (placeholder-shaped for later compatibility), the user's reason, timestamp, and an attribution field; the record persists in `$ARTIFACTS_DIR` and is also visible via `git log` (commit trailer or comment).
  ← Satisfies: "SC3 — durable audit record"
- When this story is complete, an agent (process lineage / non-interactive shell) attempting to invoke `dso commit-override` is refused with an explicit error; a user (interactive shell) succeeds.
  ← Satisfies: "SC3 — agent cannot self-authorize"
- When this story is complete, `dso commit-override` returns a non-zero exit with a clear message naming autonomous mode as the reason when the `dso-fbky` autonomous-mode flag is active.
  ← Satisfies: "SC3 — autonomous mode disables override (cross-epic constraint)"
- When this story is complete, unit tests are written and passing for all new or modified logic.
  ← Satisfies: TDD Done-of-Done

## Considerations

- [Reliability] Override token consumption must survive IDE git integrations and pre-flight dry-run hook invocations. Token validity bound to a (diff-hash, reason) tuple consumed only by the matching commit — not consumed by any hook execution that doesn't culminate in a successful commit.
- [Reliability] Three-way interaction: when `dso-fbky` autonomous mode is active AND `review.max_resolution_attempts` is exhausted AND a verifier-blocking artifact gap is present, the agent halts with a structured signal that the orchestrator surfaces on the next user-interactive turn — do not silently retry.
- [Maintainability] Audit record schema must be forward-compatible with the wrapper artifact / breadcrumb schema introduced by Story 2 (and aligned with PRECONDITIONS attestation per a154-98de). Pick a minimal stable schema now; Story 2 builds on it.
- [Security] Override path must compose with — not bypass — reviewer override discipline (cross-epic with `jira-dig-1673`); user-invoked override produces an audit record both gates can consume.
- [Maintainability] Audit record includes attribution metadata fields (skill name, agent ID, sub-agent context) consumable by `e407-d35c` source attribution.

## Escalation Policy

**Escalation policy**: Proceed unless a significant assumption is required to continue — one that could send the implementation in the wrong direction. Escalate only when genuinely blocked without a reasonable inference. Document all assumptions made without escalating.
data.title: As a developer, I can override a blocked compliance-verifier commit interactively with an audit trail
